intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Mississippi County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: During our evaluation, nothing came to our attention that would warrant disclosure in this report.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated February 23, 2026. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Dyess
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer Although Schedule 1 of this report shows a balance of $62,147 in General Fund, it was brought to our attention that as of December 31, 2025, the General Fund owed a significant amount to the Street Fund. As shown in Note 5 on Schedule 3, when this outstanding amount was considered, the General Fund had a deficit balance of $3,249. A similar finding was noted in the previous five reports.
